svg.aria-label: The token chain, played twice. You sign in with Microsoft Entra ID as the Tier 1 Technician, then as the Senior Technician. msp-support-agent has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and no Dataverse permission. Its OAuth connection servicedesk-write obtains your token for the gateway: audience the gateway app, scope ServiceDesk.Access, object ID yours. API Management validates the token, adds x-correlation-id, forwards your object ID and adds the backend key from Azure Key Vault. The MCP server's managed identity id-mcp-123456 read that key at startup; it calls Microsoft Dataverse as its application user with CallerObjectId set to you, and Dataverse applies the intersection of your role and the application user's role. The request is update_ticket_priority on TCK-10543, from P3 Medium to P2 High. Tier 1 Technician: denied by Dataverse with PrivilegeDenied 0x80040220, nothing changed, logged as Denied by Dataverse. Senior Technician: allowed, TCK-10543 is now P2 High. Same agent, same MCP server.
svg.title: The agent acts with your permissions, never more

svg.text: Key idea The same agent and the same MCP server give the two technicians different results, because Dataverse checks the person behind every call.
